page: Amazon Web Services m6id.32xlarge is a general-purpose, high-capacity compute instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. The instance is built on dual-socket 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processors (x86_64 architecture) operating at 3.5 GHz. It provisions 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 54 MB of L3 cache, 512.0 GB of DDR4-3000 memory maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU), and a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps.

A central hardware feature of the m6id.32xlarge is the inclusion of 7,600 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD local instance storage. Unlike EBS-only configurations, this onboard storage delivers low-latency disk I/O directly over the PCI bus. In compute benchmarks, the machine achieves top-tier results in PassMark CPU score (86,368.21), PassMark Extended Instructions (105,925.53), and PassMark Encryption (110,966.13), alongside strong multi-core outcomes in stress-ng (123,862.47) and Clang software compilation (49,222.0). Cryptographic acceleration is reinforced by hardware-level AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets.

The primary tradeoff of the m6id architecture lies in its single-thread versus multi-thread scalability. While its parallel multi-core performance sits in the top 10% to 25% of benchmarks, single-core metrics fall into the median range, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,693.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1,891.58. Additionally, local NVMe storage is ephemeral by nature, requiring an external persistence layer or replication mechanism to protect data across instance stops.

Given its combination of 128 dedicated vCPUs, 512 GB of memory, 50 Gbps network bandwidth, and 7.6 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage, the m6id.32xlarge is suited for I/O-intensive databases, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, distributed data processing, CI/CD build farms, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m6id.32xlarge is a general-purpose instance driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and equipped with 64-core, 128-vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it couples 512.0 GB of DDR4-3000 memory with 7,600 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local instance storage and 50 Gbps baseline networking. While single-thread benchmarks are average, multi-threaded metrics rank in the top percentiles, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 86,368.21 and strong Clang software compilation throughput. The presence of dense local NVMe storage eliminates external EBS latency overheads for temporary storage, making this instance suitable for large relational and NoSQL databases, memory caching architectures such as Redis, distributed big data processing, and large parallel compilation workloads.
